questions.q: What is the primary difference between an informal letter and a formal letter?
questions.a: Informal letters are written to friends and family with casual language, while formal letters are for officials or businesses using specific formats. A wrong answer suggests the student hasn't grasped the purpose of the audience in communication.

questions.q: Why do we use sensory details when writing a description?
questions.a: We use them to help the reader experience the object through their imagination, making the writing feel real. A wrong answer indicates the student thinks "description" is just listing facts rather than creating an experience.

questions.q: You are writing a letter to your cousin. Write the opening greeting and the first sentence.
questions.a: "Dear [Name], I hope you are doing well." Steps: Identify the recipient, choose a warm salutation, and start with a friendly inquiry. A wrong answer shows a lack of understanding of informal tone.

questions.q: Compare the sentence "The banana is yellow" with "The banana has a smooth, yellow peel and tastes like creamy vanilla." Which is better for descriptive writing and why?
questions.a: The second sentence is better because it adds texture, color, and taste. A wrong answer shows the student struggles to identify "adding detail" as the core of description.

questions.q: If you are describing a rainy day, which set of sensory details is more effective: "It is raining and wet" or "The grey clouds rumble, the air smells like wet earth, and the water feels cold on my skin"?
questions.a: The second set is more effective because it uses sound, smell, and touch. A wrong answer suggests the student confuses general statements with specific sensory imagery.

questions.q: Write two sentences describing a fresh apple using at least two different senses.
questions.a: "The apple feels cool and smooth in my hand. When I bite it, it makes a crisp crunch and tastes sweet." A poor answer lacks sensory words or only describes the look of the apple.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Letter writing is a structured way of ______ messages to specific people, divided into informal letters for friends and family, and formal letters for officials or businesses.
Fill in the blank: Have you ever wanted to tell your best friend about a new game you found, or ______ the delicious taste of a mango to someone who has never eaten one?
What is Letter writing? State the definition given in this lesson.
questions.a: Letter writing is a structured way of communicating messages to specific people, divided into informal letters for friends and family, and formal letters for officials or businesses.

questions.q: What common mix-up does this lesson flag about Letter writing?
questions.a: Students often mistake descriptive writing for a list of adjectives.

questions.q: What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student must be able to draft an informal letter with a greeting, body, and closing, and write a paragraph describing an object using at least three distinct sensory details.
